note: The four praxis routing policies. routes are routing-tier names, not hardware; read a run's pool map for what actually served it. Keys stay A/B/C/D because summary.arm is recorded evidence. The old names all-gpu, gpu-small and gpu-split remain aliases; historical run directories keep their original names.

configs.name: one-pool
configs.behavior: Every request goes to one through-stack route: no classifier, no CPU, no failover.

configs.name: small-first
configs.behavior: Every request pins to the small route (the classifier labelled effectively everything MEDIUM, so the pin reproduces the recorded routing). Either GPU route can take over on failure.

configs.name: round-robin
configs.behavior: Alternate across CPU and GPU with no classifier.

configs.name: hybrid
configs.behavior: General and sensitive entries pin to CPU; the general entry degrades to any pool, the sensitive entry only to the approved GPU (fail closed). Judgment entries pin risk/report to the GPU.

configs.name: cap-split
configs.behavior: The hybrid policy with one route changed: liability-cap extraction goes to the CPU MoE (vllm-cpu) instead of the CUAD specialist, which stays on termination, governing law and audit rights. Measured variant for the CUAD liability-cap experiment (FINDINGS 17.2); not the default policy.
